notes: Page 2 is an intro page with no building step. A minifigure opens the box, sorts the pieces and starts building. No pieces are added.
The Claude Docs tools and the Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors were not needed. The connectors need authorizing in claude.ai connector settings before they can be used.
Step 1: black 6x8 plate is the base.
Step 2: four light bluish gray 1x4 plates form a frame around a white 2x4 grooved tile at the back of the base plate. The frame is a pinwheel of four 1x4 plates.
The manual doesn't show clearly how far the frame overhangs the base. I assumed all five pieces clutch the base plate b1.
Step 3: green 1x1 plate, tan 1x1 grooved tile, 2 black pieces and 2 long dark flat pieces go on the front of the base plate.
The two black 1x1 pieces are assumed to be black round plates (lego-6141), because the parts list has no black 1x1 plate.
The two long dark pieces are smooth on top, so I took them as dark bluish gray 1x4 grooved tiles (lego-2431) and not 1x6 plates.

Step 4: eight light bluish gray 1x1 tiles, a green 1x1 plate and a green 1x3 plate. Seven tiles go onto the base plate studs. The red arrow shows the eighth tile going onto a black stud. I assumed that stud is the second black piece, b10.
All the new pieces are assumed to sit directly on the base plate b1 (or on b10 for the last tile).

Step 5: dark bluish gray 1x6 plate, 1x1 plate and 1x4 plate trim the frame around the white tile. I assumed the frame plates b2 to b5 as the supports under them. The pinwheel layout is not clear enough to be sure which ones.

Step 6: yellow 1x2 plate, light bluish gray round 1x1 plate, dark gray 1x2 plate, reddish brown round 1x1 plate and the green flower. The 1x2 dark piece is assumed to be a dark bluish gray 1x2 plate. It could be a 1x3.
I couldn't see exactly what the yellow plate rests on, so I assumed the black round plate b9. The round plates and the flower are assumed to sit on the base plate b1.

Step 7: two red 1x3 bricks form the back wall on top of the dark 1x6 plate. Two red Technic 1x2 bricks form the right wall. Each gets a black Technic pin pushed into one pin hole, and they stick out to the right.

Step 8: two red 1x1 bricks are added at the front left of the window. The green 1x1 plate goes on a round plate, and the dark 1x1 plate goes on that. The trans-clear 1x1 brick goes next to the tan tile.
What each new piece rests on is guessed from the drawings, especially in step 8.

My page 5 and 6 part types were guessed from the drawings and may be wrong in places. Comparing the 'not yet placed' lists suggests some pieces were different from what I recorded, e.g. a light bluish gray 1x4 plate and black round plates.
Step 9: two light bluish gray 1x1 bricks go into the window area. Four trans-light-blue 1x2 plates are stacked into a tower between them (the inset shows three stacked plus the fourth added).
Step 10: dark bluish gray 1x6, 1x4 and 1x2 plates and a 1x1 plate trim the top of the red walls. A yellow 1x2 grooved tile goes on the front left.
The picture doesn't show clearly what each piece rests on. The rests_on lists are my best reading of the drawings, especially for the 1x1 dark plate, the gray bricks and the yellow tile.

Step 11: three red 1x1 bricks and a stack of three white 1x1 plates go on the dark trim. In the inset, two white plates are stacked first, then a third is added to make the stack. The stack and the two red bricks go on the left end of the back trim, with the stack between the red bricks. The third red brick goes on the back right corner.
Step 12: a red 1x1 brick, a light bluish gray 1x3 arch and a dark 1x2 plate. The arch bridges the two gray bricks at the front of the window. The red brick position is uncertain.
What each new piece rests on is a best guess from the drawings.
The white stack plates are assumed to be white 1x1 plates (lego-3024). They could be round plates.
Step 13: two black 1x1 clip plates (lego-60897) go on the right gray brick stack and on the arch. A green cone goes on the trans-clear brick at the front left.

Step 14: three stacks of three 1x2 plates are built (the inset shows two plates stacked, then a third added, 3x). I read all nine as Trans-Clear 1x2 plates (the 3x and 6x icons look different in the drawing, but the inventory has exactly 9 trans-clear ones). The stacks go on top of the left and back wall near the red bricks.
The exact supporting pieces for the clips and the stacks are a best guess from the drawings.
Step 15: red 1x1 plate, trans-clear 1x1 plate, trans-clear 1x2 plate, dark bluish gray 1x1 plate and dark bluish gray 1x2 plate go on the top of the stacks and the right wall.
Step 16: trans-clear 1x1 plate, two red 1x1 plates and a trans-clear 1x2 plate go on the top layer of the stacked walls.
Several of these icons are small and I couldn't tell the part types or positions for sure, so the types and rests_on are guesses. The 1x2 and 1x3 plates are hard to tell apart in the icons.
Step 17: three red 2x4 plates cover the top of the building as a roof.
Step 18: two dark bluish gray 1x4 tiles, two dark 1x1 tiles and a yellow 1x2 grooved tile form a tiled patch with a yellow centre on the roof.
The roof layout and which plates the tiles rest on are guesses from the drawings. The 1x1 tiles are read as dark bluish gray, since the inventory has two of those.

Step 19: a flat plate and three black cheese slopes go on the left side of the roof, with the slopes along the left back edge. I could not tell if the flat plate is a 3x3 (dark bluish gray) or the black 2x2, so I assumed the 3x3. The slopes may be on the roof edge, not on the plate.
Step 20: a light bluish gray 1x4 arch goes over the front doorway on the gray bricks. Two trans-yellow round light covers are clipped into the black clips as lamps, one each side of the arch.
What each piece rests on is a best guess.

Step 21: four red 1x1 bricks go on the dark plate on the left roof, and two dark 1x2 plates go on the arch. The inventory shows only one red 1x1 brick left, so some of these four may be a different red part.

Step 22: four stacks (inset 4x), each two trans-clear 1x1 plates topped by a white round 1x1 plate. They fill the gaps between the red bricks on the 3x3 plate. I read the 4x icon as white round plates and the 8x icon as trans-clear plates.
All the supports are guesses from the drawings.

Step 23: four red 1x2 plates (the page shows one being placed, with a 4x label) are laid across the red bricks and white-topped stacks on the left roof. I paired each with one red brick and one stack. A light bluish gray 1x2 jumper plate (one stud) goes on the arch plates at the front.
The pairing and the supports are guesses from a small drawing. The 'not yet placed' list does not show red 1x2 plates, so the type is taken from the inventory totals.

Step 24: a fire hydrant is built from a red 1x1 brick with studs on 2 sides (lego-47905). Three red round 1x1 plates go on it: one on top, one on each side stud. The finished hydrant is placed on the front of the base plate.
A dark bluish gray 3x3 plate goes on top of the red cap plates on the left roof.
The hydrant position on the base plate and the plate's supports are guesses from the drawing.
Step 25: a light bluish gray round plate goes on the jumper plate at the front arch. Four white cones and a yellow cone make a flower on the dark 3x3 roof plate, with the yellow one in the middle.
The yellow cone does not appear in the 'not yet placed' list, so the yellow piece could be another part. I assumed a yellow cone and put it on the same plate as the white ones.
Step 26: four light bluish gray 1x1 grooved tiles go on top of the four white pieces on the roof, one each, like flat petals or fan blades around the yellow centre.
A cone has no top stud, so the white pieces in step 25 may really be studded plates. I kept my earlier part types.
Step 27: four white cones go on top of the four gray petal pieces on the roof, one each.

This shows that the four white pieces I recorded in step 25 (b127 to b130) were probably white round plates (lego-6141), not cones. The inventory has only four white cones, and those are these. I can't change the earlier page, so b127 to b130 still say lego-59900.
The cones would need a stud under them, so the gray petal pieces may not be plain tiles. I kept my earlier types.
A new sub-model starts here, separate from the fire station built on pages 3 to 18.
Step 1: three white 1x3 plates are laid side by side to make a white 3x3 layer. They clutch nothing below, so rests_on is empty.
Step 2: two black 1x3 tiles lie across the three plates, perpendicular to them. Each bridges all three plates, which holds the layer together.
The small black part in the white box at the top of step 1 is not clearly shown being placed anywhere, and I couldn't identify it, so I did not add it. It may be a sub-model shown for reference.
Step 3: the third column of the 3x3 layer is filled. A red 1x1 plate goes in the middle and two black 1x1 tiles go at the ends.
I couldn't identify the red part in step 3 from the 'not yet placed' list, so I assumed a red 1x1 plate. I assumed the two dark 1x1 tiles are dark bluish gray grooved tiles (lego-3070b).

I put each of the new plates and tiles on the white plates under them. In the earlier step the white plates seemed to be 3x3 built from three 1x3 plates, so the end tiles go on the first and last of them.
Step 4: a black 2x2 plate goes on top and clutches only the red plate's stud, since tiles have no studs.
Step 5: two black 2x1 45-degree slopes go on the black 2x2 plate and form a pyramid-shaped roof. Both rest on b148.

Step 28: the finished little tower (white plates, black tiles, 2x2 plate, pyramid) is pressed onto the four pieces on the left roof of the station. No new pieces. I recorded it as joins between the tower's white plates and the four white cones, because I can't change the earlier pieces' rests_on.
Which tower plate meets which roof piece is a guess.
A new sub-model starts here: the fire truck. The parts box at the top of the page also shows parts for later steps, which I did not place.
Step 1: a white 1x2 plate is the base.
Step 2: two gray door-rail plates (lego-32028) sit on the white plate, each overhanging one end, so the rails stick out at both ends.
Step 3: a dark 1x2 plate goes across the two rail plates.

Step 4: four wheels attach to the door rails, two per rail plate. The wheel part looks like a dark round disc with a hole, which is not in the catalogue. I used dark bluish gray 1x1 plates (lego-3024) as the nearest match in the inventory, so the wheel type is a guess.
The white plate type is also a guess. The 'not yet placed' list shows no white 1x2 plate left.
Step 5: a red 1x4 plate goes on top of the chassis.
Step 6: a red clip tile at the back, a white round tile, a red 1x1 plate and a trans-dark-blue cheese slope (windscreen) at the front.
Step 7: a red cheese slope on the red 1x1 plate. A white 1x2 handle plate is clipped into the red clip, with a white 1x3 plate on it, forming a ladder swung upright.
Step 8: the ladder is folded down flat on top of the truck. No new pieces and no change in connections.
These piece identifications are guesses from small drawings, and the red parts do not match the 'not yet placed' list well. Types and positions are best readings.
A new sub-model starts here, probably a small vehicle with a windscreen and a spotlight.
Step 1: a white 1x1 grooved tile goes on the top stud of a white 1x1 brick with studs on 4 sides.
Step 2: a trans-dark-blue cheese slope goes on one side stud and a black round support on another.
Step 3: two white tooth plates go on the other side studs, and a red cheese slope goes on top of the black round support.
Which side stud takes which part is a best guess from the small drawings.
Step 4: the model is turned over and a blue Technic pin goes in the top of the white brick, like a rotor shaft.
Step 5: a dark flat plate is pressed onto the pin as a rotor blade. Step 6 shows the finished result, with the blade sitting across the top of the model.

The icons for the dark plates are small. I used the one dark door-rail plate (lego-32028) the 'not yet placed' list still shows. A second blade might be shown, but I couldn't clearly see one, so I added only one.
The pin's exact connection point is a best guess.
Page 26 has no building steps. It shows the finished fire station with the helicopter sub-model standing on its right roof and the fire truck parked beside it.
I recorded the helicopter as a loose resting contact with the roof tiles. It is a guess which roof piece it touches.

The 'not yet placed' list still shows six pieces: 1x 3024 dark bluish gray, 1x 3070b dark bluish gray tile, 1x 3623 green plate, 2x 4081b clip plates, 6141 reddish brown and 6141 light bluish gray round plates. These are probably for the last page.
Page 28 is advertising. It shows the Bricktober sets 40180 to 40183 and the combined town. No pieces or connections are added.

Six pieces from the parts list are never placed in my record: 1x lego-3024 dark bluish gray, 1x lego-3070b dark bluish gray, 1x lego-3623 green, 2x lego-4081b, and the reddish brown and light bluish gray lego-6141 round plates. Several part types from earlier pages were guesses, so this is probably a mix of my mistakes and pieces I couldn't place from the drawings.
I did not see page 27, so any building on it is missing from my record. The six unplaced pieces may belong there.

Separate groups: the booklet really builds separate models. The fire station with its tower and helicopter is one. The small fire truck is a second model parked beside it and is not attached to it. I kept it separate on purpose.

Missing parts: seven pieces from the parts list were never placed in what I recorded. They are 3024 dark bluish gray, 3070b dark bluish gray, 3623 green, two 4081b and the two 6141 reddish brown and light bluish gray round plates. I have added them now. I never saw page 27, which probably builds them, so only the green 1x3 plate has a position guess (front left of the base, under the hydrant). The other six have empty rests_on because I don't know where they go.

Part types that don't match the list: I can't change earlier pieces, so I list them here. Two 3023 plates are over-counted and are probably other parts. The four white 59900 'cones' b127 to b130 from step 25 are probably white round plates lego-6141. The four real cones are b136 to b139. One red 54200 slope is over-counted, because b164 or b173 is probably a different red part.

Overspecified rests_on: b58 (red 1x1 brick) and b145 (red 1x1 plate) list more supports than a single stud cell can have. The right ones are probably b49 for b58 and b141 for b145. Please treat the extra supports as unreliable.
Cones on tiles: b136 to b139 cannot sit on tiles with no studs. I have added joins to b127 to b130 as the likelier connection.

The leftover pieces b177 to b182 were floating with no connection, which made extra groups. I have now joined them to the station's base plate b1. The positions are guesses, since I never saw page 27, which probably builds them.

Separate groups: what remains is two groups, and that is correct. The fire station with its tower and helicopter is one model. The small fire truck is a second model that the booklet builds on its own and parks beside the station, so it is not attached. I kept it separate on purpose.

I can't change the earlier pieces, so the over-listed rests_on of b58 and b145 stay as they were. The cones b136 to b139 on tiles also stay. Their likelier supports are b49 for b58, b141 for b145, and b127 to b130 for the cones, and the last of these is in the earlier corrections.
